entities.name: Legal Codification Across Civilizations
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: The practice of compiling and organizing rules governing human conduct into systematic written codes. From the Code of Hammurabi in Mesopotamia to the Twelve Tables of the Roman Republic, Justinian's Digest, and Napoleon's codification efforts, societies have repeatedly sought to reduce the complexity of social norms into authoritative written collections that could be consulted, taught, and enforced by specialized officials.
